sample_rule.rule: Every lang/en.json key whose text (placeholders removed) holds a digit (set A, 77 keys); every English prose string of config.mjs with a digit, found by importing config.mjs in node and walking its exported tables (set B, 13 strings); every lang/en.json key whose text holds a number word two..twelve, twice, thrice, double or half, not already in A (set C, 60 keys); every lang/en.json key whose text says 'press' or 'Press', not in A or C (set D, 46 keys). 196 rows. Each row was read against the code or config that holds its number or its button.
sample_rule.count_note: 196 rows sampled; 122 traced to the code or config that holds the number or the button (59 'agrees, number typed', 22 'agrees', 40 'button or window exists', 1 'differs'); 56 read and set aside as no rule number (a count of clicks, walls, rooms or ends; a plural's .one form; a name like Stage 6 or tier 2 of the suite); 18 not traced (versions, the system's own rule, tier tables' amounts, two controls that name themselves). The 'press' scan's label matcher was a regex: its seven misses were read by hand and all resolved (Back to the debate, Convert to passages, Ask for the opening roll again, Close and count).

gm_only_scan.rule: The audience map (tools/text-audience.mjs's buildAudienceMap, run from /tmp) gives 1422 keys a reader other than the GMs; of those, the 658 whose readers include a card to a player (owner, everyone, incident, room, one, list) were scanned for 33 sensitive nouns and placeholders (killer, Blackened, Mastermind, victim, body, stash, hidden, Monocub, Key Remnant, answer key, unfound, Overflow, pool, witness, trap, passage, secret, planned, Faint, Reinforced, threshold, 'only GMs', {band}, {owner}, {who}, {pool}, {count} ...) and for GM windows named to a player (GM panel, Students window, Season setup, Despair Flow, trial console, Incident tracker, Diagnostics): 83 + 62 + 7 hits, every one read with its sender; and all 138 keys sent to everyone or a room were read.
gm_only_scan.read: 152 keys read with their sending code; 4 findings (1 and 4 here; 2 and 3 are table 3.1's); 3 refuted (the Bounty's debt lines, a masked name in a tail's or a watch's card, the Eclipse refill count); 1 recorded as a decision (the assembly).

findings.title: A death kept by the GMs during an incident sends the GMs' note 'Only the GMs know of this death ... in the Students window' to the incident's players
findings.where: scripts/death.mjs:257-293 (deathAudience, the card); lang/en.json:3290 DRPG.Chapter.keptUntilFound, :3276 DRPG.Chapter.vaultPending; lang/pl.json:3500
findings.what_happens: recordDeath posts its card with whisperToGms, but hands it the whisper list deathAudience: the GMs and incidentAudienceIds(state) while an incident runs (death.mjs:257-262). With `secretly` true - the victim of the running incident (death.mjs:176) - the card carries DRPG.Chapter.keptUntilFound, a GM's note: 'Only the GMs know of this death until the body is found or a GM makes it known in the Students window. The table sees nothing yet: no marker, and the student's Truth Bullets are still on the sheet.' The players of the incident's seats (the killer, the victim, a third) read it. To them the first clause is not true (they were there), and the rest is the GM's procedure and a fact about the victim's sheet.
findings.failure_scenario: A killer's player finishes a direct murder; their chat shows 'A character dies ... Only the GMs know of this death until the body is found or a GM makes it known in the Students window', a note written for the GM, about a death they caused.
findings.expected: The style guide's surface matrix (docs/text-style.md section 3): a GM card holds no line to a player and a player card no GM procedure (O19, T29); the incident's players get the death's facts, the GMs the note.
findings.refutation_tried:
Checked whisperToGms (utils.mjs:762-767): extra.whisper replaces gmIds(), so the incident's owners are readers. Checked that `secretly` and an incident coincide: secretly defaults to isIncidentVictim (death.mjs:176) and deathAudience is non-null only with murderState() (death.mjs:259-261). The card is veiled (its words to the readers alone), which does not take the note out of a reader's copy: the GM prose cut (secret.mjs:335) takes .drpg-gm-only, and the note is a plain

. No test or scenario names DRPG.Chapter.keptUntilFound or vaultPending (git grep over scripts/tests*.mjs and audit/harness). The audience tool reads this send as 'gms/list' and does not name the incident.

findings.title: The planner's Key Remnant note says ordinary evidence is 'three to six points harder'; for an Obvious Remnant of daily life it is two
findings.where: lang/en.json:3077 and lang/pl.json:3314 (DRPG.Investigation.keyDcNote); drawn at scripts/investigation.mjs:940-947; scripts/config.mjs:1147-1152 (OBSERVE_DC)
findings.what_happens: The note's list of Key Remnant thresholds is read off OBSERVE_DC (investigation.mjs:941-946, 'so the sentence cannot drift from the rule it describes'), but its next sentence is typed: 'Ordinary evidence in the same band is three to six points harder to notice.' OBSERVE_DC.obvious is { dailyLife: 8, key: 6, ... }: two points. The other bands and columns give 3 to 6 (evident 12 vs 9, subtle 18 vs 12, hidden 21 vs 15; prep and incident 3 above key in each band; faint 6 above).
findings.evidence:
config.mjs:1148  obvious: { dailyLife: 8, key: 6, faint: 12, prep: 9, incident: 9, resolution: 9 },
config.mjs:1149  evident: { dailyLife: 12, key: 9, ... },
investigation.mjs:941  // Read off OBSERVE_DC so the sentence cannot drift from the rule it
en.json:3077  "... Ordinary evidence in the same band is three to six points harder to notice. ..."
pl.json:3314  "... Zwykły dowód o tej samej widoczności ma próg wyższy o trzy do sześciu. ..."
findings.failure_scenario: A GM planning a chapter reads that ordinary Obvious evidence is at least three points harder than an Obvious Key Remnant, and judges an Obvious clue's ease against 9 when the room's ordinary Obvious traces are seen at 8.
findings.expected: The difference read off OBSERVE_DC as the list above it is, or a range that holds for every band and column (two to six).
findings.refutation_tried: Considered whether 'ordinary evidence' means only the prep and incident columns (3 in every band): the daily-life column is the ordinary Remnant of a Search or an Observe outside an incident (Observe's daily-life ladder, per old-1.2.42-text TEXT-14 tests-tier0.mjs:13702-13730), and faint is 6, so the reading 'every non-key column' gives 2 to 6. No test names keyDcNote (git grep over scripts/tests*.mjs).

findings.title: The Rot says 'everything the living carry' wears down; it also wears what is in their stash
findings.what_happens: rotEverything walks `actor.items` of every living character and wears each item that has a spare point; it asks isBroken, never isStashed. In the module's own words 'carried' leaves the stash out (inventory.mjs:711 'Everything on them that can do this job, stash excluded.'), and the Polish says 'każdy przedmiot, który nosi ktoś żywy'. The GM handbook's Overflow table (gm-handbook.en.md:583) says 'every item', which is what the code does.
findings.failure_scenario: A player who stashed a tool to keep it safe reads the Rot's card ('everything the living carry'), and later finds the stashed tool one point more worn.
findings.expected: One fact in both places (O3): the card says what the code wears - every item a living student has, stash included - or the Rot leaves the stash alone.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a stash filter on the Rot's road: itemAsHeld returns the GMs' item (sheet-audit.mjs) and the loop's only skip is broken/last point; config.mjs:2686-2694 describes the Rot as 'Every durable thing in the school' and 'everything with a durability track', so the code is meant to wear the stash too; the sentence is the narrower one.

findings.title: A player is told the GM's answer key is missing and how a GM restores it from a backup
findings.where: lang/en.json:3602 (DRPG.Handover.answerKeyMissing), lang/pl.json:3867; sent at scripts/handover.mjs:279-281 and scripts/trial.mjs:404 (whisperToOwner)
findings.what_happens: When a Truth Bullet's real type is not on the GM that runs a share or a presentation, the player whose action it was gets 'Nobody can get a copy of “{name}” now: the GM's record of what it really is has gone missing. The GM can restore it from a backup (GM panel, Diagnostics, The case: Restore from a file).' - a store, a GM window and its path, in a player's card.
findings.failure_scenario: A player presents a Truth Bullet in the trial after a GM's browser lost the case store, and reads that 'the GM's record of what it really is' is gone and the GM's menu path to restore it.
findings.expected: O19 and T29 (docs/text-style.md section 2): a player's text says what happened and what they keep; the GM's procedure goes to the GMs' copy (whisperToOwner sends one, utils.mjs) or a GM card.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked the audience: whisperToOwner (text-audience 'owner', with the GMs' copy), both senders; no .drpg-gm-only wrap. Not a secret (the existence of a hidden real type is the rule of Analyze), so category text, not leak. The same old row (3.4-06, Hud.trialTooltip) was judged harmless and left for a rewrite.

by_decision.what: A Public Announcement's gather leaves a body nobody has found where it lies (call-world.mjs:497-502 isDeadForGm), and its public card counts the tokens moved ('{n} characters were moved to {room}', call-world.mjs:433-437, lang/en.json:4140): the table sees one student fewer at the assembly before the discovery. The refill at an Eclipse counts by the table's knowledge for that very reason (actions.mjs:434-439, 'one that skipped a body nobody has found would name it').

(in the section on an undiscovered body); old DESP-15 (audit/findings-1.2.42/despair.md:215-224, 'Body tokens are evidence: moving one also moves the crime scene'). strengths: Numbers come from config through placeholders in the sentences 1.2.42 found wrong: every one of the 18 rows of table 3.1 now reads its number off the rule, or the key is gone (3.1-01..3.1-18).

One cut for every private card: the GM prose class (secret.mjs:335) and a masked killer's name (secret.mjs:448-500 wordsFor, maskNames) are taken out per reader, so a tail's or a watch's card naming who stands in a room (tail-gm.mjs:131-134, watch-gm.mjs:107-109) gives '?' for a mask without a rule of its own.
The Eclipse's public refill count is the table's knowledge, not the GMs' (actions.mjs:434-439), so it does not count a body nobody has found.
A Monocub Bounty's debt line goes to the GMs alone (monocub.mjs:1791-1797 tellBounty: the cubs get the public line, the GMs it and the gmOnly line).
Of 46 sentences that say 'press <button>', 40 name a label that exists in en.json with that text, on the window they name where checked (sample set D).
